ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: `EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false` (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden by this unit. The sim's `Encounter` (monsters/base.py) is a plain dataclass with no `on_*`/hook-listener interface at all -- it is never registered with `HookSystem` (grep `hooks.register` across sts2_rl/: only `Creature.__init__`/`Monster.__init__` call it) -- so it architecturally cannot receive a combat hook, matching the false default by construction rather than by an explicit flag. Faithful.

This unit passes no `min_gold`/`max_gold` override to its sim `Encounter`, so `generate_combat_rewards` (rewards.py:885-887) falls through to the room-type default range -- matching the C#'s own inheritance of the base ladder.

guards.what: Per-encounter Rng independence (EncounterModel.cs:41-49's own doc comment: the encounter's Rng is independent of the run's centralized Rng, safe because its state need not survive past the encounter)
guards.rationale: Stream IDENTITY (which Rng object, how it is seeded) is `seam/rng_streams`'s mechanism, not this record's -- cited, not re-verdicted, per PROMPT.md rule 3 and this batch's brief. What IS this record's to check: does the sim's draw actually land on that independent per-encounter Rng rather than a shared/run-level one? `sts2_rl/run.py:1609-1613`'s `create_combat` builds `encounter_selection_rng` via `make_encounter_rng(seed, total_floor, encounter.entry)` (rng.py, verdicted faithful by seam/rng_streams step 21) whenever `self.rng_set is not None` (parity mode -- string- seeded runs, the conformance/replay path) and threads it into `CombatState`/`Encounter.create_monsters` as `selection_rng` (combat.py:222-223). In that mode the draw this record verdicts lands on the correct independent stream. When `rng_set is None` (legacy mode -- `run.py:1609`'s own comment: 'Legacy runs pass None and keep their random.Random composition draws', the RL-training path: `grep -n rng_set sts2_rl/run_env.py` returns zero hits, so training never sets it), `selection_rng` is None and the draw falls back to the shared legacy `random.Random` -- the game's independence guarantee is not honoured in that mode. This is the SAME sim-wide, already-documented parity-vs-legacy split every other RNG consumer in this codebase carries (seam/rng_streams's own G2-adjacent discussion of `CombatRng`'s legacy fallback), not a defect specific to this encounter, and it does not affect the conformance/replay path this campaign's own symptom (89U21BV1TZ) is measured against. Checked per this batch's brief instruction; not filed as a new gap.
